name: North Carolina
agency: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles (NCDMV), NC Department of Transportation
permitAge: 15 (Level 1 limited learner permit, ages 15 to 17), after driver education (G.S. 20-11)

teen.supervisedHours: Statute: 60 hours with at least 10 at night for Level 2, then 12 hours (6 at night) for Level 3. Possibly changed in 2025-2026 (HB 584 / SL 2026-46); not confirmed. Not used in questions.
teen.holdPermit: Sources disagree (9 months in the handbook vs 12 months in secondary sources); not used in questions
teen.nightLimit: Level 1: first 6 months only 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. with a supervisor, then any time with a supervisor. Level 2: alone 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.; 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. needs a supervisor except driving directly to or from work, or volunteer fire, rescue or EMS
teen.passengerLimit: Level 2 without a supervisor: no more than one passenger under 21, unless all passengers are household members; under-21 household members may not ride with an under-21 non-household member
teen.phone: Under 18: no mobile phone use at all while driving, hands-free included, except calls to a parent, legal guardian, spouse or emergency services. All drivers: no texting or reading texts while moving.

bac.under21: any detectable amount (zero tolerance), secondary source

notes: Supervising driver: licensed at least five years, seated beside the driver in the front seat; parent, grandparent or adult approved by a parent or guardian (NCDMV, DL-214).
Level 3 full provisional removes the time, supervision and passenger limits of Levels 1 and 2 (DL-214).
Knowledge test: secondary sites mostly say 25 questions, 20 correct (80 percent), with a separate sign section; others say 37/30 or 20/75 percent. Not confirmed on NCDMV; left null.

Driving Eligibility Certificate requirement reported eliminated effective October 1, 2026 (SL 2026-46); DL-214 was revised 06-26. Log and holding-period rules may have changed; re-check before writing questions on them.

School bus (news and DMV flyer): two-lane roads, two-lane with center turn lane and four-lane without median: all traffic stops; divided highway of four or more lanes with a median: only traffic following the bus stops. One news report mentions HB 7 effective July 15, 2026; effect not confirmed.
Move Over Law (G.S. 20-157): move over a lane or slow down and be prepared to stop (NCDOT). Fine about $250 (secondary).
Spanish handbook: a 2014 news report says NCDMV published the handbook in English and Spanish; current Spanish URL not confirmed.
